data.content_ref: inline:The claim effectively asserts a lower bound of 23 for R(3,3,3) over Q and quadratic number fields — surpassing the best known proved lower bound of 19 — yet the derivation array is empty and the mechanism consists entirely of unproven assertions presented as established facts. Three specific leaps are stated without any formal lemma or proof: (1) 'the 22 rank-1 terms cannot be partitioned into orbits whose sizes sum to 22 while preserving the trilinear identity over Q' — no orbit-stabilizer calculation is shown; (2) 'the Galois conjugate of any valid decomposition would give a second distinct valid decomposition' — distinctness is assumed, not proven, and the possibility of a self-conjugate decomposition (fixed by Galois) is not ruled out; (3) 'the tensor's known degeneracy structure forbids two conjugate decompositions from both being rank-minimal' — no such 'known degeneracy structure' is identified or cited. This is a conjecture dressed as a proven obstruction. Furthermore, the predictions (a) bounded-denominator search finds no rank-22, (b) ALS approaches but never certifies 22, (c) solution exists mod p without lifting, are all experimentally testable, yet no sandboxed simulation is filed — the problem explicitly requires filed simulations for such discriminating predictions and states that prose-only claims will be criticized.
